title: Prakrama 3, Sarga 5. The Breaking of the Staff
html:
The Lord travels towards Purushottama with His companions, singing the names of Rama and Krishna; the toll-collectors; Nityananda breaks the Lord's sannyasa staff, and the Lord, feigning anger, admits that He has done His will

Verse 1

ततः प्रतस्थे भगवान्मुकुन्द-
गदाधराद्यैर्द्विजसज्जनैः प्रभुः।
पुरोऽवधूतं प्रणिधाय देवो
रराज काव्येन यथोडुपेशः॥१॥

tataḥ pratasthe bhagavānmukunda-
gadādharādyairdvijasajjanaiḥ prabhuḥ|
puro'vadhūtaṁ praṇidhāya devo
rarāja kāvyena yathoḍupeśaḥ||1||

tatah — then; pratasthe — set out; bhagavan — Bhagavan; mukunda-gadadhara-adyaih — with Mukunda, Gadadhara and the rest; dvija-sajjanaih — virtuous brahmanas; prabhuh — the Lord; purah — in front; avadhutam — the Avadhuta; pranidhaya — placing; devah — the Lord; raraja — shone; kavyena — with Kavya (Venus); yatha — as; udu-peshah — the lord of the stars (the moon).

1Then Bhagavan, the Lord, set out with Mukunda, Gadadhara and other virtuous brahmanas; placing the Avadhuta in front, the Lord shone like the moon, the lord of the stars, beside Kavya1.

Verse 2

गच्छन्क्वचिद्गायति कृष्णगीतं
क्वचिद्वदेदर्थमलब्धसंज्ञम्।
क्वचिद्द्रुतं याति शनैः क्वचित्स्खल-
द्गतिः क्वचित्प्रेमविभिन्नधैर्यः॥२॥

gacchankvacidgāyati kṛṣṇagītaṁ
kvacidvadedarthamalabdhasaṁjñam|
kvaciddrutaṁ yāti śanaiḥ kvacitskhala-
dgatiḥ kvacitpremavibhinnadhairyaḥ||2||

gachchhan — going; kvachit — at times; gayati — sings; krishna-gitam — a song of Krishna; kvachit — at times; vadet — utters; artham — a sense; alabdha-samjnam — that finds no name; kvachit — at times; drutam — quickly; yati — goes; shanaih — slowly; kvachit — at times; skhalat-gatih — with stumbling gait; kvachit — at times; prema-vibhinna-dhairyah — His composure shattered by love.

2As He went, at times He sang a song of Krishna, at times He uttered something indistinct for which there were no words; at times He walked fast, at times slowly, at times stumbling, and at times His composure was shattered by love.

Verse 3

सायं क्वचिद्भक्ष्यमुपस्थितं भवे-
त्तदन्नमश्नाति हरिर्यथाविधि।
रात्रौ च गायत्यथ रौति धैर्यं
विसृज्य देवो महतां सुखाय॥३॥

sāyaṁ kvacidbhakṣyamupasthitaṁ bhave-
ttadannamaśnāti hariryathāvidhi|
rātrau ca gāyatyatha rauti dhairyaṁ
visṛjya devo mahatāṁ sukhāya||3||

sayam — in the evening; kvachit — somewhere; bhakshyam — food; upasthitam — offered; bhavet — happens to be; tat — that; annam — food; ashnati — eats; harih — Hari; yatha-vidhi — according to rule; ratrau — at night; cha — and; gayati — sings; atha — and; rauti — cries out; dhairyam — restraint; visrijya — casting aside; devah — the Lord; mahatam — of the great souls; sukhaya — for the joy.

3If in the evening some food happened to be offered somewhere, Hari ate it according to the rule. And at night the Lord cast aside all restraint and sang and wept, to the joy of the great souls.

Verse 4

स्वयं पपाठ भगवाञ्श्लोकमेकं शृणुष्व तम्।
यं श्रुत्वा तत्पदाम्भोजे रतिः स्यादनपायिनी॥४॥

svayaṁ papāṭha bhagavāñślokamekaṁ śṛṇuṣva tam|
yaṁ śrutvā tatpadāmbhoje ratiḥ syādanapāyinī||4||

svayam — Himself; papatha — recited; bhagavan — Bhagavan; shlokam — verse; ekam — one; shrinushva — hear; tam — it; yam — which; shrutva — hearing; tat-pada-ambhoje — for His lotus feet; ratih — attachment; syat — will be; anapayini — unfailing.

4Bhagavan Himself would recite one verse — hear2 it: whoever hears it will gain unfailing attachment to His lotus feet:

Verse 5

राम राघव राम राघव राम राघव पाहि माम्।
कृष्ण केशव कृष्ण केशव कृष्ण केशव त्राहि माम्॥५॥

rāma rāghava rāma rāghava rāma rāghava pāhi mām|
kṛṣṇa keśava kṛṣṇa keśava kṛṣṇa keśava trāhi mām||5||

rama — O Rama; raghava — O Raghava; pahi — protect; mam — me; krishna — O Krishna; keshava — O Keshava; trahi — save; mam — me.

5"Rama, Raghava, Rama, Raghava, Rama, Raghava, protect me! Krishna, Keshava, Krishna, Keshava, Krishna, Keshava, save me!"

Verse 6

एवं कलपदं गायन्हसंस्तत्त्वविदां वरः।
इमान्सुशिक्षयँल्लोकाँल्लोकानां पालकोऽव्ययः॥६॥

evaṁ kalapadaṁ gāyanhasaṁstattvavidāṁ varaḥ|
imānsuśikṣaya~llokā~llokānāṁ pālako'vyayaḥ||6||

evam — thus; kala-padam — sweetly; gayan — singing; hasan — smiling; tattva-vidam — of the knowers of truth; varah — the best; iman — these; su-shikshayan — instructing well; lokan — people; lokanam — of the worlds; palakah — the protector; avyayah — the imperishable.

6So, sweetly singing and smiling, the best of the knowers of truth, the imperishable protector of the worlds, gave fine instruction to these people.

Verse 7

पथिकान्याचकान्दृष्ट्वा क्वचिद्दानी समागतः।
आहूय तान्निवृत्तोऽभूत्स्वयमेव गतक्लमः॥७॥

pathikānyācakāndṛṣṭvā kvaciddānī samāgataḥ|
āhūya tānnivṛtto'bhūtsvayameva gataklamaḥ||7||

pathikan — travellers; yachakan — mendicants; drishtva — seeing; kvachit — once; dani — a toll-collector; samagatah — who had come up; ahuya — calling out to; tan — them; nivrittah abhut — turned back; svayam eva — of his own accord; gata-klamah — his weariness gone.

7Once a toll-collector came up; seeing that they were mendicant travellers, he called out to them — and then turned back of his own accord, as if relieved of a burden3.

Verse 8

कदाचिदपरो दानी पथि गत्वा जगद्गुरुम्।
वारयामास दानार्थी यात्रिकाणां गणैर्वृतम्॥८॥

kadācidaparo dānī pathi gatvā jagadgurum|
vārayāmāsa dānārthī yātrikāṇāṁ gaṇairvṛtam||8||

kadachit — once; aparah — another; dani — toll-collector; pathi — on the road; gatva — approaching; jagat-gurum — the Guru of the world; varayam asa — stopped; dana-arthi — demanding the toll; yatrikanam — of pilgrims; ganaih — by crowds; vritam — surrounded.

8Another time a different toll-collector, demanding the toll, came out onto the road and stopped the Teacher of the world, who was surrounded by crowds of pilgrims.

Verse 9

तमाह भगवान्गच्छ दूरं त्वं करसंज्ञया।
ततोऽगच्छत्तदानीं स भगवान्मुदितो ययौ॥९॥

tamāha bhagavāngaccha dūraṁ tvaṁ karasaṁjñayā|
tato'gacchattadānīṁ sa bhagavānmudito yayau||9||

tam — to him; aha — said; bhagavan — Bhagavan; gachchha — go; duram — away; tvam — you; kara-samjnaya — with a sign of the hand; tatah — then; agachchhat — went off; tadanim — at once; sah — he; bhagavan — Bhagavan; muditah — joyful; yayau — went on.

9Bhagavan said to him, "Go away!" with a sign of His hand. The man left at once, and Bhagavan went on joyfully.

Verse 10

अवधूतकरे दण्डं दत्त्वा स्वीयं जगद्गुरुः।
अग्रे जगाम च पश्चान्नित्यानन्दः शनैर्ययौ॥१०॥

avadhūtakare daṇḍaṁ dattvā svīyaṁ jagadguruḥ|
agre jagāma ca paścānnityānandaḥ śanairyayau||10||

avadhuta-kare — into the Avadhuta's hand; dandam — the staff; dattva — giving; sviyam — His own; jagat-guruh — the Guru of the world; agre — ahead; jagama — went; cha — and; pashchat — behind; nityanandah — Nityananda; shanaih — slowly; yayau — walked.

10Once the Teacher of the world gave His staff into the Avadhuta's hand and walked on ahead, while Nityananda walked slowly behind.

Verse 11

दूयमानेन मनसाचिन्तयत्स उदारधीः।
अहं विहरमाणोऽसौ प्रभुर्मे दण्डधारकः॥११॥

dūyamānena manasācintayatsa udāradhīḥ|
ahaṁ viharamāṇo'sau prabhurme daṇḍadhārakaḥ||11||

duyamanena — pained; manasa — with a mind; achintayat — thought; sah — he; udara-dhih — the noble-minded; aham — I; viharamanah — roam at pleasure; asau — while this; prabhuh — Lord; me — my; danda-dharakah — bears the staff.

11With an aching heart the noble Nityananda thought, "I roam at will, and my Lord carries a staff!

Verse 12

असौ श्रीभगवान्साक्षाद्दृश्यते प्रज्वलन्नलम्।
शङ्खचक्रगदापद्मधरो देवः श्रियान्वितः॥१२॥

asau śrībhagavānsākṣāddṛśyate prajvalannalam|
śaṅkhacakragadāpadmadharo devaḥ śriyānvitaḥ||12||

asau — He; shri-bhagavan — Sri Bhagavan; sakshat — directly; drishyate — is seen; prajvalan — blazing; alam — intensely; shankha-chakra-gada-padma-dharah — holding conch, discus, club and lotus; devah — the God; shriya — with Shri; anvitah — accompanied.

12For He is Sri Bhagavan Himself: I see Him with my own eyes, blazing brightly — the God who holds the conch, discus, club and lotus, together with Shri.

Verse 13

लौकिकीं दर्शयंश्चेष्टां न्यासदण्डधरो हरिः।
मुरलीवादनः पूर्वं जगन्मोहनरूपकः॥१३॥

laukikīṁ darśayaṁśceṣṭāṁ nyāsadaṇḍadharo hariḥ|
muralīvādanaḥ pūrvaṁ jaganmohanarūpakaḥ||13||

laukikim — customary in the world; darshayan — displaying; cheshtam — conduct; nyasa-danda-dharah — bearing the staff of renunciation; harih — Hari; murali-vadanah — the player of the flute; purvam — formerly; jagat-mohana-rupakah — whose form enchants the world.

13And here is Hari following the customs of this world and carrying the staff of renunciation — He who once played the flute, whose form enchants the world,

Verse 14

राधारसविलासी च श्रीहरेः सन्निधौ स्थितः।
तं दृष्ट्वा प्राह भगवान्दण्डं मे देहि माचिरम्॥१४॥

rādhārasavilāsī ca śrīhareḥ sannidhau sthitaḥ|
taṁ dṛṣṭvā prāha bhagavāndaṇḍaṁ me dehi māciram||14||

radha-rasa-vilasi — who sported in rasa with Radha; cha — and; shri-hareh — of Sri Hari; sannidhau — near; sthitah — having come to stand; tam — him; drishtva — seeing; praha — said; bhagavan — Bhagavan; dandam — the staff; me — to Me; dehi — give; ma-chiram — without delay.

14who sported in rasa with Radha!" With such thoughts He came up beside Sri Hari. Seeing Him, Bhagavan said, "Give Me the staff — quickly."

Verse 15

अवधूतस्ततः प्राह दैवाद्भूमौ पदं मम।
प्रस्खलत्तेन दण्डस्ते भग्नो भीत्येत्युवाच सः॥१५॥

avadhūtastataḥ prāha daivādbhūmau padaṁ mama|
praskhalattena daṇḍaste bhagno bhītyetyuvāca saḥ||15||

avadhutah — the Avadhuta; tatah — then; praha — said; daivat — by chance; bhumau — on the ground; padam — foot; mama — my; praskhalat — slipped; tena — thereby; dandah — staff; te — Your; bhagnah — broke; bhitya — in fear; iti — thus; uvacha — spoke; sah — he.

15Then the Avadhuta said, "By chance my foot slipped on the ground, and with that Your staff broke." So He spoke, in fear.

Verse 16

ततश्चुकोप भगवानवधूतं जगाद च।
दण्डे मे संस्थिता देवाः शिवाद्याः सहशक्तयः॥१६॥

tataścukopa bhagavānavadhūtaṁ jagāda ca|
daṇḍe me saṁsthitā devāḥ śivādyāḥ sahaśaktayaḥ||16||

tatah — then; chukopa — grew angry; bhagavan — Bhagavan; avadhutam — to the Avadhuta; jagada — said; cha — and; dande — in the staff; me — My; samsthitah — reside; devah — the gods; shiva-adyah — headed by Shiva; saha-shaktayah — together with their shaktis.

16And Bhagavan grew angry and said to the Avadhuta, "In My staff reside the gods headed by Shiva, together with their shaktis4.

Verse 17

तेषां पीडां विधाय त्वं बभञ्ज मम दण्डकम्।
देवपीडाकृतं दोषं नो जानासि किमल्पकम्॥१७॥

teṣāṁ pīḍāṁ vidhāya tvaṁ babhañja mama daṇḍakam|
devapīḍākṛtaṁ doṣaṁ no jānāsi kimalpakam||17||

tesham — to them; pidam — pain; vidhaya — causing; tvam — you; babhanja — broke; mama — My; dandakam — staff; deva-pida-kritam — arising from causing pain to the gods; dosham — the sin; no janasi — do you not know; kim — whether; alpakam — (it is) slight.

17You have caused them pain and broken My staff. Do You not know that the sin of causing pain to the gods is no small thing?"

Verse 18

तच्छ्रुत्वा प्राह तं देवो हितं तेषां कृतं मया।
ततः क्षणात्त्यक्तरोषो भगवानिदमब्रवीत्॥१८॥

tacchrutvā prāha taṁ devo hitaṁ teṣāṁ kṛtaṁ mayā|
tataḥ kṣaṇāttyaktaroṣo bhagavānidamabravīt||18||

tat — that; shrutva — hearing; praha — said; tam — to Him; devah — the divine one (Nityananda); hitam — good; tesham — for them; kritam — done; maya — by me; tatah — then; kshanat — in a moment; tyakta-roshah — His anger gone; bhagavan — Bhagavan; idam — this; abravit — said.

18Hearing this, the divine Nityananda answered Him, "I have done them good"5. And in a moment Bhagavan let go of His anger and said,

Verse 19

गत्वा च श्रीजगन्नाथं दृष्ट्वा श्रीपुरुषोत्तमम्।
स्थित्वा कतिपयं मासं पार्श्वे श्रीचक्रिणो मया॥१९॥

gatvā ca śrījagannāthaṁ dṛṣṭvā śrīpuruṣottamam|
sthitvā katipayaṁ māsaṁ pārśve śrīcakriṇo mayā||19||

gatva — having gone; cha — and; shri-jagannatham — to Sri Jagannatha; drishtva — having seen; shri-purushottamam — Sri Purushottama; sthitva — having stayed; katipayam — some; masam — months; parshve — beside; shri-chakrinah — the Holder of the discus; maya — by Me.

19"After going to Sri Jagannatha, seeing Sri Purushottama and staying some months beside the Holder of the discus,

Verse 20

न्यासो दण्डस्य कर्तव्यो ममासीन्मतिरीदृशी।
तमसौ च बभञ्जोर्व्यां क्षिप्तवान्किं करोम्यहम्॥२०॥

nyāso daṇḍasya kartavyo mamāsīnmatirīdṛśī|
tamasau ca babhañjorvyāṁ kṣiptavānkiṁ karomyaham||20||

nyasah — the laying down; dandasya — of the staff; kartavyah — was to be done; mama — My; asit — was; matih — intention; idrishi — such; tam — it; asau — he; cha — but; babhanja — broke; urvyam — to the ground; kshiptavan — threw; kim — what; karomi — can do; aham — I.

20I was to lay down the staff — that was My intention. But He has broken it and thrown it on the ground. What am I to do now?"

Verse 21

इत्युक्त्वा तं क्रोडीकृत्वा प्रोवाच मधुराक्षरम्।
मदभिप्रायमेव त्वं कर्तुमर्हसि सर्वदा॥२१॥

ityuktvā taṁ kroḍīkṛtvā provāca madhurākṣaram|
madabhiprāyameva tvaṁ kartumarhasi sarvadā||21||

iti — thus; uktva — saying; tam — him; krodi-kritva — taking into His embrace; provacha — said; madhura-aksharam — in sweet words; mat-abhiprayam — My intention; eva — just; tvam — you; kartum arhasi — should carry out; sarvada — always.

21So saying, He took Him into His embrace and spoke sweetly: "You must always carry out just what I intend"6.

Thus ends the fifth sarga, "The Breaking of the Staff" (Danda-bhanjana), of the third prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. Kavya is the planet Venus (Shukra). Nityananda, walking in front, is compared to Venus, the Lord to the moon.
  2. The narrator, Murari, is addressing Damodara (see Sarga 3.1).
  3. Literally "his weariness gone": on seeing the Lord and His companions, the toll-collector apparently gave up his greed of his own accord.
  4. Shaktis are divine energies, the consorts of the gods.
  5. That is, He has set free the gods confined in the staff.
  6. The Lord admits that by breaking the staff Nityananda has only carried out His own innermost wish.
